request_state.context: New this session: (i) fixed-base closures via rank-0 curves for {3,4,r} and (3,3,r), all r at once; (ii) fixed-three-bases covering sieve: all pairwise-coprime triples with bases <= 80 have no solution with exponents >= 3 (two implementations agree to N=50). Neither closes a signature. Open core unchanged. Tools: Lean4, PARI/GP, Python.

next.instructions: Which next step has the best chance of producing a statement stronger than 'small bases'?

criteria.scale_sieve: keep scaling the base bound (N=120, 200) — tests H_N but is more of the same
criteria.two_bases_fixed: fix only TWO bases (A,B) and let C vary: A^x + B^y = C^z, x,y,z>=3 — a genuinely stronger statement; look for a covering argument in (x,y) that forces A^x+B^y to be a non-perfect-power (e.g. via its residues mod many primes being non-z-th-powers for every z)
criteria.one_base_fixed_general: fix ONE base for general signatures using the covering idea rather than genus-1 curves
criteria.lean_certificates: build a Lean certificate checker so the sieve results become kernel-checked
criteria.structure_of_shadows: study the shadow phenomenon: every hard triple shadows a true identity with an exponent < 3; conjecture and test: 'a triple is undecidable by pure covering iff it shadows such an identity' — links the sieve to the Fermat-Catalan list
